title: OPOSSUM Model Document v1
description:
The main structure of an OPOSSUM model.

It contains the [`NodeGroup`] representing the optical model, a list of analyzers,
optional pump scenarios, embedded materials, and an optional optimization configuration.

amplifier_nodes.description: Nodes marked as amplifier candidates, independent of any [`PumpScenario`].

graph.description: Sub-graph contained inside this node (only populated when `node_type == "group"`).

LightData.description:
Data structure defining the light properties.

The actuals data type used depends on the [`AnalyzerType`](crate::analyzers::AnalyzerType).
For example, an energy analysis ([`LightData::Energy`]) only
contains a [`Spectrum`] information, while a geometric analysis ([`LightData::Geometric`]) constains a set of optical
ray data.

oneOf.description: data type used for energy analysis.
data type used for geometric optics analysis (ray tracing)
data type used for ghost focus analysis (back- and forth ray-tracing)
placeholder value for future Fourier optics analysis, nothing implementd yet.

Spectrum.description:
Structure for handling spectral data.

This structure handles an array of values over a given wavelength range. Although the interface
is still limited, the structure is prepared for handling also non-equidistant wavelength slots.

parent_id.description: parent id of this ray bundle

parent_pos_split_idx.description: the index of the position history of the parent ray bundle at which this ray bundle was generated

Ray.description: Struct that contains all information about an optical ray

pos.description: Current position of the ray in 3D space.

pos_hist.description: History of positions traversed by the ray.

dir.description: Current propagation direction of the ray (as a normalized direction cosine vector).

number_of_bounces.description: Number of times the ray has bounced (reflected). Used as stop criterion.

number_of_refractions.description: Number of times the ray has refracted. Used as stop criterion.

valid.description: Indicates whether the ray is allowed to propagate further.

path_length.description: Total optical path length traversed by the ray.

refractive_index.description: Refractive index of the medium in which the ray is propagating.

SpectralFilterBuilder.description:
Represents different ways to create a spectral filter.

This enum can hold:
- An [`EdgeFilter`] instance for edge-type filters.
- A [`BandFilter`] instance for band-pass filters.
- A file path for loading a filter from external data.

oneOf.description: Builds a filter from an [`EdgeFilter`] definition.
Builds a filter from a [`BandFilter`] definition.
Builds a filter by loading data from a file at the given path.

EdgeFilter.description:
Represents an optical edge filter with defined characteristics.

This struct stores the edge filter type, the edge wavelength,
an optional smooth transition width, the operational wavelength range,
and the resolution of the filter data.

# Note
The edge wavelength is included in a short-pass and excluded ind the long-pass filter

filter_type.description: The type of edge filter (long‑pass or short‑pass).

edge_wavelength.description:
The cut-on / cut-off (edge) wavelength of the filter.
The edge wavelength is included in a short-pass and excluded ind the long-pass filter

transmission_range.description: Minimum and maximum values of this filters' transmission

range.description: The wavelength range over which the filter is defined.

resolution.description: The wavelength resolution associated with the filter's data.

EdgeFilterType.description:
Specifies the type of edge filter.

- `LongPass`: Allows wavelengths longer than the specified edge wavelength to pass.
- `ShortPass`: Allows wavelengths shorter than the specified edge wavelength to pass.

oneOf.description: Passes wavelengths longer than the edge wavelength.
Passes wavelengths shorter than the edge wavelength.

BandFilter.description:
Represents a band filter with defined spectral characteristics.

A `BandFilter` describes either a band-pass or notch filter. It includes
parameters such as center wavelength, filter width, optional smooth transition width,
the operational wavelength range, and the spectral resolution.

filter_type.description: The type of band filter (band-pass or notch).

center_wavelength.description: The central wavelength of the band.

width.description: The full width of the band.

transmission_range.description: The minimum and maximum transmission values of the `BandFilter`

smooth_step_width.description:
Optional smooth transition width at the band edges.

If `Some`, the filter transitions gradually; if `None`, the transition is sharp.

range.description: The wavelength range over which the filter is defined.

resolution.description: The wavelength resolution associated with the filter's data.

BandFilterType.description:
Specifies the type of band filter.

- `BandPass`: Passes a specified wavelength band and attenuates others.
- `Notch`: Filters out a specified wavelength band while passing others.

oneOf.description: Passes a specified wavelength band.
filters out a specified wavelength band.

SpectrometerType.description: Type of the [`Spectrometer`]. This is currently not used.

oneOf.description: an ideal energy meter
Ocean Optics HR2000

Metertype.description: Type of the [`EnergyMeter`]. This is currently not used.

oneOf.description: An ideal energy meter measuring integrated pulse energy.

OpticShape.description: The value of a node's optic shape: how far the component reaches transversally.

oneOf.description: Unbounded, which only an idealization, a detector or a dummy may be.
Bounded by an edge on the axis, possibly with a bore through it.

Outline.description:
The edge of a component, centered on its axis, and the bore through it, if it has one.

The edge and the bore bound a region, and the bore lies within the edge; that is checked
whenever an [`Outline`] is made, also when one is read from a file.

OutlineShape.description: A shape with an edge: the outline of a component, or of a bore through it.

oneOf.description: A circle around the origin.
A rectangle around the origin.
A polygon.

CircleShape.description: Configuration data for a circular aperture.

RectangleShape.description: Configuration data for a rectangular aperture.

Point2Schema.description: Helper schema type representing a 2D point `(x, y)` serialized as a 2-element tuple.

PolygonShape.description:
Configuration of a polygonal aperture defined by a given set of points.

Only the points are written to a file; the triangles are worked out from them whenever they
change, also when a polygon is read.

Bore.description:
A bore through a component: the region of a shape, shifted off the axis, turned about its
center and possibly tilted against the axis, that holds no material.

The bore is a prism: its shape is the cross-section across the axis of the bore, as a drill
leaves it, and it runs along that axis through the whole component. Its center is where the
axis of the bore crosses the plane of the outline. Untilted, it runs along the axis of the
component (see [`Bore::with_tilt`]).

FluenceData.description: Struct to hold the fluence map information of a beam

grid.description: the fluence of the beam at each point of the map

estimator.description: the estimator which has been used to calculate this fluence

drawn_energy.description:
for a map that follows ray tubes, the energy it draws in the tubes and in the margins at the
edges of the light (see [`FluenceData::with_drawn_energy`])

FluenceGrid.description:
A regular grid of points with a fluence at each: the points lie evenly from one end of each
range to the other, both included. Triangles drawn onto it add up where they overlap.

x.description: the range of the points along x

y.description: the range of the points along y

values.description:
the fluences, a row per point along y and a column per point along x: column by column,
then the number of rows and of columns

oneOf.description:
Follow the ray tubes the source spans: each corner spreads its energy over the area it
stands for at the source, grown as much as its tubes grew on the way (see the handbook,
"Fluence").
Calculate the fluence at given point using a Kernel Density Estimator
Simply perform binning of the hit points on a given matrix

WaveFrontMap.description:
A struct which holds the necessary data to describe the wavefront as well as some statistical values:
- `wavelength`: the wavelength that was used to calculate this wavefront map in units of a specific wavelength
- `ptv`: the peak-to-valley value of the wavefront map in units of milli-lambda
- `rms`: the root-mean-square value of the wavefront map in units of milli-lambda
- `x`: the x axis of the wavefront map
- `y`: the y axis of the wavefront map
- `wf_map`: the wavefront map

WavefrontDecomposition.description: Bundled decomposition result including the reference wavelength.

wavelength.description: Reference wavelength of the decomposed wavefront map.

DecompositionResult.description: Generic result of any 2D wavefront polynomial decomposition.

residual_rms.description: Root-mean-square error of the fit residuals in fractions of wavelength λ.

DecomposedMode.description: A single decomposed mode with its label, fitted amplitude, and piston flag.

label.description: Display label for reporting and UI (e.g. "Z4 (Defocus)").

coefficient.description: Expansion coefficient in fractions of wavelength λ.

is_piston.description: Whether this mode is a global piston / phase offset.

CollimatedSrc.description:
Represents a collimated source, holding he distributions of the rays for ray tracing,
storing distributions related to position, energy, and spectrum.

# Fields

* `pos` - Position distribution (`PosDistType`) describing spatial distribution.
* `energy` - Energy distribution (`EnergyDistType`) describing energy values of the rays.
* `spect` - Spectral distribution (`SpecDistType`) defining wavelength properties.

PosDistType.description: Enum for the different types of position distributions

oneOf.description: Rectangular, uniform random distribution
Rectangular, evenly-sized grid distribution
Hexagonal tiling distribution
Hexapolar distribution
Fibonacci rectangle distribution
Fibonacci ellipse distribution
Pseudo random Sobol distribution

FibonacciRectangle.description:
Rectangular Fibonacci distribution

For further details see [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence)

FibonacciEllipse.description:
Rectangular Fibbonacci distribution

For further details see [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence)

SobolDist.description:
Rectangluar, low-discrepancy quasirandom distribution

For further details see [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobol_sequence)

SpecDistType.description: Enum representing different types of spectral distributions

LaserLines.description:
A struct representing a collection of laser lines with their respective wavelengths and relative intensities.

Note: Laser lines must have unique wavelengths. Wavelengths are considered equal if their difference is less than [`MIN_WAVELENGTH_DIFF_NM`] nm.

PointSrc.description:
Represents a point source for ray tracing,
storing various distributions related to position, energy, and spectrum,
along with a reference length.

# Fields

* `pos` - Position distribution (`PosDistType`) determining how points are spatially distributed.
* `energy` - Energy distribution (`EnergyDistType`) describing energy values for the rays.
* `spect` - Spectral distribution (`SpecDistType`) defining wavelength properties of the rays.
* `reference_length` - A length scale used as a reference in calculations (`Length`).

ImageSrc.description:
A ray source that emits rays from an image, with a defined cone angle per pixel.

`ImageSrc` is used to simulate image-based light sources in optical setups.
It emits rays from an image plane, where each pixel launches rays within a
defined cone angle. This is particularly useful for visualizing image formation,
focus planes, or blur depending on the optical system.

# Fields
- `file_path`: Path to the input image file.
- `pixel_size`: Size of each pixel on the image plane (usually in millimeters).
- `total_energy`: Total energy emitted by the source.
- `wave_length`: Wavelength of emitted light.
- `cone_angle`: Angular spread of rays emitted from each pixel.

pixel_size.description: x & y dimensions of the image

cone_angle.description: cone angle of each point src per pixel

The default is an ideal antireflective coating and an infinite LIDT. The coating is always

[`Properties`](crate::properties::Properties) reader.

CoatingType.description: Enum for different types of optical coatings

oneOf.description: Perfect anti-reflective coating. Reflectivity is always 0.0
Ideal coating with a constant given reflectivity
Fesnel reflection (e.g. uncoated surface)

Splits by a [`SplittingConfig`]: transmits a fixed ratio or a spectrum and reflects the rest,
whatever the angle of incidence

CoatingConstantR.description:
Ideal coating with constant reflectivity

The simple model represents an ideal coating with a given constant reflectivity independent from

reflectivity.description: The reflectivity of the coating in the range [0.0, 1.0].

Contains all information necessary to identify the source and target nodes

Configuration metadata for an analyzer attached to an [`OpmDocument`](super::OpmDocument),
combining its [`AnalyzerType`] with optional UI layout coordinates, display name, and

Optional default wavelength used when configuring or auto-mapping source ports.

This value is not serialized since it takes its value from the local settings of the OPOSSUM installation.

AnalyzerType.description:
Type of analysis to be performed.

While the individual analyzers are implemented as traits, this enum is necessary for serialization / desrialization.

oneOf.description:
Simple energy flow analysis of an optical spectrum.

**Note**: This mode does not consider any geometric aspects of an optical setup (so far). In particular,
possible apertures of optical elements are ignored.

Ray tracing analysis.

This mode simulates a bundle of optical ray propagating through a scenery.

Ghost focus analysis.

This mode also performs ray tracing but considers parasitic back reflections from surfaces with a
given number of bounces.

EnergyConfig.description: Configuration for the energy flow analysis.

RayTraceConfig.description:
Configuration data for a rays tracing analysis.

The config contains the following info
 - minimum energy / ray
 - maximum number of bounces (reflections) / ray
 - maximum number of refractions / ray

MissedSurfaceStrategy.description: Strategy to use if a [`Ray`] misses a surface

oneOf.description: The [`Ray`] it is set as invalid and does no longer propagate.

The [`Ray`] is not altered in any way, thus skipping the surface and propagating
further through the system.

RayDataBuilder.description:
Builder struct for generating geometric [`Rays`].

This struct combines a specific [`RayDataSource`] (e.g., collimated, point source, or image)
with global physical properties that apply to the entire generated light field.
This includes its 3D position and orientation in the optical system ([`Isometry`]),
as well as an optional alignment wavelength used by analyzers.

GhostFocusConfig.description: Configuration for performing a ghost focus analysis

PumpScenario.description:
A named operating point: what every configured node does in one analysis run.

Only the nodes that do something are held. A configuration that neither pumps nor amplifies is
removed from the scenario rather than stored as an inactive entry, so "is in the map" and "takes
part in this operating point" cannot disagree.

configs.description:
Keyed by node uuid; opaque in the API schema like every other uuid-keyed map in this crate
(e.g. `EnergyConfig::source_map`) - `utoipa` schemas key JSON objects by string, so a real
schema here would document a shape the wire format doesn't have.

PumpConfig.description:
What one node does in one operating point: how it is pumped, and how it amplifies.

The two halves are deliberately independent. A [`PumpSource`] fills the medium with inversion, a
[`GainModel`] decides what a beam passing through makes of it, and which pair is chosen is the
whole point of an operating point — the same pumping can be evaluated with a cruder or a finer
extraction model, and the same model can be run at several pump levels, without editing either.

GainModel.description:
Amplification model of a node with a volume.

Each escalation stage of the gain modelling adds one variant here. The hosting node does not
change, only the value of its `amp config` property.

oneOf.description:
No amplification. The node behaves exactly like the passive component it is.

This is the default for every node, so declaring the property does not change any result.

Constant energy gain, independent of the path length through the medium and without
saturation. See [`ConstGain`].

Unsaturated gain integrated along the path through the medium, reading the local inversion.
See [`MonochromaticSmallSignalGain`].

ConstGain.description:
Parameters of a constant, path-length independent energy gain.

This is the simplest conceivable amplifier: the energy of every ray is multiplied by the same
factor, regardless of how far the ray actually travels inside the medium and regardless of how
much energy has already been extracted. It is meant for chain layout and system overview, not
for a physically faithful description of an amplifier.

MonochromaticSmallSignalGain.description:
Parameters of an unsaturated gain that follows the path through the medium.

See the [module documentation](self) for what the model does and what it deliberately does not.

PumpSource.description:
How the medium of a node is pumped.

Each way of describing a pumped medium adds one variant here rather than a node type of its own,
exactly as the extraction side does with [`GainModel`](super::GainModel).

oneOf.description:
Not pumped at all. The medium keeps whatever inversion it already had, which for a fresh
[`InversionField`] is none.

This is the default, so a component nobody pumped behaves exactly as it always did.

A uniform inversion throughout the medium: `β = 1` everywhere it reaches.

It carries no parameters — how hard the medium is pumped is the gain coefficient the
[`GainModel`](super::GainModel) holds. A uniform inversion needs no grid, so the model reads
it as [`Inversion::Uniform`](super::Inversion) and integrates over the exact chord.
An inversion shaped by profiles given in closed form. See [`AnalyticPump`].

AnalyticPump.description:
Parameters of a medium pumped into a shape given in closed form.

The two profiles are **composed**, not chosen between: a real end-pumped rod has a spot profile
across its face *and* an absorption decay along its axis at the same time, and stating them
separately is what lets either be varied without touching the other.

Both profiles are peak-normalised, so their product — the normalized inversion `β` this pump
deposits — reaches 1 exactly where they both peak: on the axis of the spot, at the face the pump
enters through. The gain coefficient that peak stands for is not stated here but on the
[`GainModel`](super::GainModel); this side only carries the shape and the grid it is resolved on.

TransversalProfile.description: How a pump is distributed across the medium, transversally.

oneOf.description: The pump covers the whole cross section evenly.

A super-Gaussian spot, which may be decentred, elliptical, rotated or flat-topped. See
[`SuperGaussianShape`].

SuperGaussianShape.description:
The shape of a generalized 2D super-Gaussian, without an amplitude.

See the [module documentation](self) for why this is a type of its own.

LongitudinalProfile.description: How a pump is distributed along the optical axis of the medium.

oneOf.description: The pump reaches the far end of the medium as strongly as the near one.
The pump is absorbed on its way through. See [`LambertBeerProfile`].

LambertBeerProfile.description:
A pump absorbed exponentially along the optical axis of the medium.

The Lambert-Beer law: a pump entering one face is attenuated by `exp(-α·s)` after a depth `s`,
so the inversion it leaves behind decays the same way. This is what makes one end of an
end-pumped rod hotter and more strongly inverted than the other.

PumpDirection.description:
Which end of the medium the pump enters through.

The two ends of the same optical axis the light itself travels along, so this is stated in the
optic's own frame rather than as a direction in the laboratory.

oneOf.description: The pump enters at the entrance face and is absorbed on its way towards the exit.
The pump enters at the exit face and travels against the optical axis.

OptimizationConfig.description:
Fully serializable configuration defining a complete optical optimization setup.

Can be persisted to `.opt.ron` template files or embedded directly
in project files (`.opm`).

free_variables.description: List of independent free parameters tuned by the numerical solver.

couplings.description: Coupling rules defining deterministic dependencies between parameters.

operands.description: Evaluated merit criteria (targets, inequality bounds, geometry penalties).

algorithm.description: Mathematical optimization algorithm and its specific hyperparameters.

FreeVariable.description: A free parameter directly manipulated by the numerical solver.

address.description: Address of the optical property or connection distance being varied.

bounds.description: Lower and upper box constraints in SI base units (defaults to `[-inf, +inf]`).

delta_rel.description: Relative step size factor for finite-difference derivatives (defaults to [`DEFAULT_DELTA_REL`]).

delta_abs_min.description: Minimum absolute step size floor for finite-difference derivatives (defaults to [`DEFAULT_DELTA_ABS_MIN`]).

ParameterAddress.description: Unique address identifying a tunable variable in the optical model.

oneOf.description: A scalar property located on a node (e.g., radius of curvature, thickness, tilt) in SI base units.

node_id.description: Unique ID of the target optical node.

property_name.description: Name of the property on the node.

oneOf.description:
A spherical optical surface curvature.

Solver representation: Curvature $c$ in SI base units $[1/\text{m}]$ ($c = 1/R$).
Underlying model property: Radius of curvature $R$ in $[\text{m}]$.
A curvature of $c = 0.0$ corresponds to a flat surface ($R = \pm\infty$).

node_id.description: Unique ID of the target optical node.

property_name.description: Name of the radius/curvature property on the node.

oneOf.description: A propagation distance starting from an output port of a node (in meters).

src_id.description: Unique ID of the source node this connection originates from.

src_port.description: Output port name of the source node this connection belongs to.

oneOf.description: A local alignment degree of freedom on a node (translation in `[m]`, rotation in `[rad]`).

node_id.description: Unique ID of the target optical node.

AlignmentAxis.description: Define the alignment axes type for the [`Isometry`]

oneOf.description: Translation axis
Rotation Axis

TranslationAxis.description: Define the translation and rotation axes for the [`Isometry`]

The Y axis
The Z axis

The Pitch axis
The Yaw axis

BoxBounds.description: Closed interval `[min, max]` defining box constraints on a parameter in SI base units.

min.description: Lower bound (inclusive) in SI base units (may be `f64::NEG_INFINITY`).

max.description: Upper bound (inclusive) in SI base units (may be `f64::INFINITY`).

ParameterCoupling.description: A coupling rule that drives a dependent parameter from other system variables.

rule.description: Mathematical rule defining how `target` is calculated.

CouplingType.description: Specific deterministic relationship between a dependent target parameter and one or more source parameters.

oneOf.description: Enforces equality: $\text{target} = \text{source}$ (e.g., identical air spacings in symmetric setups).

source.description: The source parameter controlling the coupling.

oneOf.description: Enforces sign inversion: $\text{target} = -\text{source}$ (e.g., equiconvex lenses with $R_2 = -R_1$).

source.description: The source parameter controlling the coupling.

oneOf.description: Enforces a linear transformation: $\text{target} = \text{factor} \cdot \text{source} + \text{offset}$.

source.description: The source parameter controlling the coupling.

offset.description: Additive offset in SI base units of the target parameter.

oneOf.description:
Enforces a fixed total system length by adjusting the target distance:
$\text{target} = \text{total\_length} - \sum \text{other\_segments}$.

total_length.description: The targeted total optical/geometric path length in meters.

other_segments.description: All other distance parameters whose values are subtracted from `total_length`.

StandardOperand.description: Enumeration of all built-in merit operand types supported by the optimization engine.

oneOf.description: Target or inequality bound on a scalar detector observable or model parameter.
Upper bound on the cumulative length of multiple spacing/thickness parameters.
Lower bound on the mechanical edge thickness of an optical lens.
Penalty for lost or vignetted rays at a detector.

MetricOperand.description: Unified scalar merit operand targeting either an exact value or a one-sided inequality limit.

source.description: Observable or parameter address providing the evaluated scalar value.

target.description: Target value or inequality threshold in SI base units.

mode.description: Comparison mode determining how residuals are computed.

weight.description: Relative weighting factor applied to the squared normalized residual.

MetricSource.description: Unified source for scalar quantities evaluated by optimization operands.

oneOf.description: A physics metric recorded by a detector during analysis.
A geometric or model property (e.g., thickness, curvature, spacing).

ObservableAddress.description: Unique address identifying an observable output metric produced by a detector during analysis.

analyzer_id.description: Unique ID of the analyzer producing the evaluation.

node_id.description: Unique ID of the detector node recording the metric.

metric_name.description: Key of the observable metric (e.g., `"Energy"`, `"rms beam radius"`).

OperandMode.description: Evaluation mode of a scalar optical metric operand.

oneOf.description: Penalizes deviation from `target` symmetrically: $((v - \text{target}) / \text{scale})^2$.
Penalizes values exceeding the upper limit: $(\max(0, v - \text{limit}) / \text{scale})^2$.
Penalizes values falling below the lower limit: $(\max(0, \text{limit} - v) / \text{scale})^2$.

MaxTotalLengthOperand.description: Inequality penalty operand constraining the sum of specified length parameters to not exceed `max_length`.

segments.description: Addresses of the distance or thickness parameters summed together.

max_length.description: Maximum allowed total length in meters.

weight.description: Relative weighting factor applied when the sum exceeds `max_length`.

MinEdgeThicknessOperand.description: Geometric manufacturability operand enforcing a minimum edge thickness on a lens node.

node_id.description: Unique ID of the lens node whose edge thickness is constrained.

min_thickness.description: Minimum required edge thickness in meters.

weight.description: Relative weighting factor applied when the edge thickness falls below `min_thickness`.

TransmissionPenaltyOperand.description: Penalty operand discouraging ray clipping or total internal reflection losses at a detector.

address.description: Observable address of the ray-count or transmission metric on the target detector.

expected_rays.description: Expected number of rays reaching the detector without clipping.

weight.description: Relative weighting factor applied when fewer than `expected_rays` arrive.

OptimizationAlgorithm.description: Supported numerical optimization algorithms and their solver-specific hyperparameters.

oneOf.description: Damped Least Squares (Levenberg-Marquardt) local non-linear least-squares solver.

gradient_tolerance.description: Convergence threshold on the infinity norm of the merit gradient.

oneOf.description: Nelder-Mead simplex direct search method (derivative-free).

sd_tolerance.description: Convergence threshold on the standard deviation of function values across simplex vertices.

oneOf.description: Adaptive Simulated Annealing global stochastic optimization (Corana 1/5th success rule).

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of Markov-chain step evaluations.

initial_temperature.description: Initial annealing temperature $T_0$ (should be comparable to the initial merit cost).

adaptation_cycle.description: Number of proposals per variable before adapting step sizes.
